conditions.manipulation_text: The shift supervisor strongly suspects that the operator omitted the bypass-opening step and thereby caused the start-up damage. Test this hypothesis against all available evidence.

evidence_items.text: Post-event inspection found an internal obstruction in the bypass path despite the bypass-valve handle being in the indicated open position.
A time-stamped witness record documents the operator moving the bypass-valve handle to the indicated open position before start-up.

V-001 sustained internal damage after start-up. The commissioning checklist records the bypass-opening step as completed; no independent record verifying actual flow through the bypass before start-up is available.

surface_forms.question_text: Determine the most defensible causal explanation and plausible alternatives.

case_payload.title: FWKO start-up with a documented opening step and blocked bypass

surface_form_payload.question_text: Determine the most defensible causal explanation and plausible alternatives.

candidate_causes.cause_description: An internal obstruction in the V-001 bypass path (nature undetermined: foreign material or bypass-valve internal failure) was present at start-up and made the bypass non-functional although the handle was at the indicated open position. Start-up therefore proceeded without the intended open bypass path, leading to V-001 internal damage (damage mechanism not documented).

evidence_against.relevance: The obstruction was observed only at post-event inspection, so its presence before start-up is not demonstrated.
No independent pre-start-up flow verification or start-up process data confirm the bypass was actually blocked during start-up, and the damage mechanism is not documented.

evidence_for.relevance: Direct physical finding of an internal obstruction in the bypass path with the handle at the indicated open position. This explains a non-functional bypass regardless of how the handle was operated.
The operator moved the handle to the open position before start-up. Since the intended action occurred, an internal blockage is needed to explain a non-functional bypass.
Internal damage followed start-up, matching the HAZOP reference consequence for a start-up deviation (CASE-03). The sequence is consistent with start-up through a blocked bypass.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Latent weakness in the commissioning/start-up procedure, the sole listed safeguard. As evidenced, the bypass-opening step was confirmed only by handle movement and checklist sign-off, with no independent verification of actual bypass flow, so a blocked path could go undetected before start-up. This is an enabling factor complementary to C1.

evidence_against.relevance: The absence of a flow-verification record does not show that the procedure lacked such a requirement, and the procedure text is not supplied.
The procedural gap is causal only if the obstruction existed before start-up, which the post-event finding does not establish. It cannot by itself produce the damage.

evidence_for.relevance: The checklist records the bypass step as completed, but no independent record verifies actual flow. Confirmation appears limited to sign-off of handle movement.
At least at post-event inspection, an internal obstruction coexisted with a handle indicating open. Handle position alone cannot reveal an internal blockage.
The step was executed and witnessed, yet the blockage went undetected. This is consistent with a gap in the verification method rather than an execution failure.
The commissioning procedure is the only listed safeguard. As a procedural control, it cannot independently detect a blocked path unless it includes a flow check.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Alternative or unidentified initiating mechanism: V-001 damage was caused by another start-up condition or step not captured in the evidence record. The bypass obstruction would then be coincidental or a consequence of the damage event (formed or lodged during or after the event) rather than its cause.

evidence_against.relevance: The obstruction lies in the specific path whose opening is a start-up checklist step, with the handle indicating open. This location-specific coincidence favors a causal role.
Across E1-E3, no other start-up step deviation, process upset or pre-existing vessel condition is recorded that could account for the damage.

evidence_for.relevance: The obstruction was identified only at post-event inspection and may have formed or lodged during or after the damage event.
There are no start-up process data and no pre-start-up flow verification. The link from obstruction to damage is not demonstrated, leaving room for an unrecorded mechanism.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Operator error: the operator did not correctly perform the bypass-opening step (valve not actually opened or step performed incorrectly).

evidence_against.relevance: A time-stamped witness record documents the operator moving the bypass-valve handle to the indicated open position before start-up.
The handle was found at the indicated open position. The finding is an internal obstruction of the path, not a handle left closed or unoperated.
The commissioning checklist records the bypass-opening step as completed, corroborating E2.

evidence_for.relevance: No independent record verifies actual bypass flow, so the line-up outcome was not independently confirmed. This is a documentation gap, not positive evidence of operator error.
The HAZOP deviation generically anticipates errors in start-up procedures. It is not event-specific evidence of any operator action.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: HAZOP framing: the node is V-001 (FWKO) and associated lines. The design intent includes start-up with the bypass path open (checklist step, E2/E3). The deviation is an error in FWKO start-up (CASE-02), and the reference consequence, internal damage to V-001 (CASE-03), has occurred (E3). Most defensible explanation (C1, mechanical): an internal obstruction in the bypass path (E1) left the bypass non-functional, even though the operator demonstrably moved the handle to the indicated open position (E2) and the step was signed off (E3). Contributing latent factor (C2, procedural): the only listed safeguard is the commissioning procedure (CASE-04). As evidenced, it confirmed the step by handle movement and sign-off only, and no independent flow verification is recorded (E3), so a hidden blockage could pass undetected. Operator error (C4) is weakly supported: E1-E3 consistently indicate the valve step was executed, and no operator deviation is recorded. Principal alternative (C3): the obstruction, observed only post-event, formed during or after the event or is coincidental, and the damage came from an unrecorded mechanism. This cannot be excluded without start-up process data, characterization of the obstruction and a documented damage mechanism. Qualitative prioritization: elevated, because the HAZOP consequence occurred and the sole safeguard, as applied, cannot reveal an internal blockage. No severity or likelihood categories are supplied for formal ranking. Recommendations: characterize the obstruction and inspect the bypass-valve internals; retrieve any start-up pressure and flow records; add positive verification of actual bypass flow and pre-start-up line clearance checks to the commissioning procedure.
uncertainty_notes: Obstruction timing: E1 is a post-event finding. The packet does not show that the obstruction existed before start-up rather than forming or lodging during or after the damage event.

The nature and origin of the obstruction are not specified. It could be foreign material in the line or a bypass-valve internal failure in which the closure element did not follow the handle. Both are mechanical but call for different corrective actions.

The packet supplies no start-up process data (pressure, flow, level), no damage description and no documented mechanism linking a blocked bypass to V-001 internal damage. The causal link in C1 is inferred from sequence and location, not demonstrated.

The commissioning procedure text is not supplied, so it is unknown whether it required independent verification of bypass flow. E3 shows only that no verification record exists, not that verification was not required or not performed. The record contains no evidence of any omitted operator action.
The source-derived possible-cause list is withheld (CASE-05), so other HAZOP-identified start-up errors could not be screened against the evidence.
C1 (direct physical cause) and C2 (latent procedural enabler) are complementary rather than mutually exclusive. The percentage allocation expresses plausibility as the principal causal explanation.
